# Payouts list

Figma: [08c. Payouts list](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=3618-122305) · Family: 08 Safqah-Specific · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-08-03

The list row used across dividends & payouts - one scheduled or completed distribution. Ten Property-1 states (Upcoming, Done · Payout, Done · Capital, Early paid, Disabled Early paid, Late, Defaulted, Partially repaid, Partially repaid closed, Partial principal) × RTL/LTR = 20 variants. Partially repaid / Partial principal are compound accordions nesting smaller payout rows.

### Payouts cell

One distribution row in a payouts list: amount and date, project name and distribution type with status suffix, and a state icon; ten states cover upcoming, received, early paid, skipped, late, defaulted and partial repayments.

Level: molecule · Contains: Alert

Use when:
- Payouts list, deal page or wallet rows grouped by year with running totals
- Late and Defaulted distributions with day counts
- Partial repayments as nested accordions; Disabled Early paid with an explanatory Alert

Don't use when:
- For the deal lifecycle use DealTimeline
- For expected pre-investment payouts use Calculator / Installment row or Distribution-schedule
- Never wrap each row in its own card; stack rows with dividers

Accessibility: State is icon plus text suffix plus colour, never colour alone; accordions expose expanded state.

Compliance: Show defaulted and late honestly (text/error for Defaulted only); keep skipped rows visible and explain early repayment profit was settled.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Payouts cell renders a single distribution in a payout or dividend list: how much, for which project, what kind (periodic vs. capital), when, and its current state.

On Safqah, cells stack into lists grouped by year, each group led by a header and a right-aligned running total - used across the Payouts list, deal pages, and the wallet.

### At a glance

### Anatomy

Left: amount (with currency mark) over the date. Right: project name over the distribution type, followed by the state icon. Mirrored in LTR.

### Parts

- Amount - distribution value; muted when pending, brand-green when received.
- Date - settlement / due date (Early paid shows both due and paid dates).
- Project - the deal the distribution belongs to.
- Distribution type - “Periodic” or “Capital”, with a status suffix (✓ received / ✓ early payment / late N days).
- State icon - loading · badge ✓ · clock · loading-circle.

### States

Ten states cover the distribution lifecycle. State is carried by the Property 1 variant - it drives the amount colour, the status icon, and the subtitle. Beyond the original six: Defaulted (distressed), Partial distribution (a nested accordion of sub-payouts, open / closed), and Partial principal (the same accordion for capital repayments).

### Upcoming

Scheduled, not yet paid - muted amount, spinner icon.

### Done · Payout

Periodic distribution received - brand-green amount, ✓ badge.

### Done · Capital

Capital returned - brand-green amount, ✓ badge.

### Early paid

Settled ahead of schedule - ✓ “early payment”, shows both dates.

### Disabled Early paid

The scheduled payout is skipped because the investment was repaid early - the row is muted and struck through (“Skipped • investment completed early”). A DS Alert (from the Alert component) sits directly below it, explaining why the payout is disabled: the investment was repaid early, so this scheduled payout wasn’t made, and profit for the actual days invested was already calculated and settled at the same fixed annual return rate. The Alert is toggleable via the Show alert boolean.

### Late

Overdue - muted amount, clock icon, “late N days”.

### Defaulted

Distribution in default - unlikely to be paid. Escalates “Late”: red amount (text/error) and red clock (icon/error), subtitle “توزيعات دورية • متعثرة / Periodic distribution • Defaulted”.

### Partial distribution - open

A grouped, expandable payout shown open. The header carries the paid count and combined total (“1 of 3 payouts paid” · 3,630); an inset bg/surface list reveals each sub-payout - paid (green ✓) and upcoming (spinner). For staged / instalment repayments. An optional info Alert can sit below the accordion (toggle the Show alert boolean) to explain the staged repayment.

### Partial distribution - closed

The same group collapsed to its header - total + paid count only, chevron pointing to expand (‹ in RTL, › in LTR). The accordion’s closed toggle state; opening it reveals the nested sub-payouts.

### Partial principal

The same accordion pattern for capital / principal repayments rather than periodic distributions. The paid sub-row becomes Done · Capital and the wording shifts to “Principal repayment”; the header subtitle reads “Principal • Total”. Also available collapsed (same mechanics as the distribution accordion).

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Every state ships RTL (Arabic, primary) and LTR (mirrored). Amount + date lead on the reading-start side; the state icon trails.

### LTR - mirrored

### In context - the payout list

Cells stack into a list grouped by year, each group led by a header and a right-aligned running total. Use dividers between rows - never wrap each row in its own card.

### Code examples

Render a single distribution; the list wrapper handles grouping and totals.

```typescript
<PayoutsCell
  state="done-payout"   // upcoming | done-payout | done-capital | early-paid | disabled-early-paid | late
  dir="rtl"
  amount={1210}
  currency="SAR"
  project="Buruj Riyadh #6"
  type="periodic"       // periodic | capital
  date="2024-03-29"
/>
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios.

Do

Keep one distribution per row and stack them into a list grouped by year, each group led by a header and a right-aligned running total.

Do

Pair the state icon with its text label and amount colour so “received” vs. “pending” is unambiguous - never colour alone.

Don’t

Don’t rely on the amount colour to carry state on its own - keep the icon (clock / badge / spinner) and the text suffix.

Don’t

Don’t wrap each row in its own card; a payout list is a single grouped list with row dividers, not a stack of cards.

### Notes from the maintainer

A few decisions worth carrying forward when extending this component:

> **Tip:** Status lives inline - the distribution type carries the suffix (✓ received / ✓ early payment / late N days). Keep it there; don’t add a separate badge column.

> **Info:** Amount colour (muted vs. brand-green) is the fastest state cue, but it must always be backed by the icon and the text label - never colour alone.

> **Info:** When a deal completes early, remaining scheduled rows switch to the disabled “completed early” state instead of being removed, so investors still see the full plan.

> **Warning:** The cell’s Arabic is set in IBM Plex Sans Arabic, which can’t load in this plugin environment - previews in this doc are exported PNGs and the reference frames the live component in place.
